_comment: The ingestion service's real output for anthropic-sdk-python's migration guide to 1.0.0, read 2026-10-17 and dumped from its store with the row id as `id`. One breaking package_release removed_parameter event per parameter the release removed from `messages.create()` and its siblings; `source_url` is MIGRATION.md at the v1.0.0 tag. `previous_version` (`0.125.0`, the release before 1.0.0 on PyPI) was added on 2026-11-20, when the contract made it required for every change found by comparing two versions. Rewritten 2026-11-21 when the contract named sources by their provider/source id: `api` is the id, every fingerprint recomputed over it with the same detail, and the event's subject as the server writes it.

changes.description: Parameter temperature removed from `messages.create()` and its sibling methods in the anthropic SDK 1.0.0: passing it raises a TypeError.
changes.migration_hint: Remove them. Current models do not use these sampling parameters; for an older model that still does, pass them through `extra_body` (see below). Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/v1.0.0/MIGRATION.md
changes.source_excerpt:
## Removed: deprecated request parameters
| Method(s)                                                                                                                                                                                       | Removed parameter               | Use instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `messages.create()`, `messages.stream()`, `messages.parse()` and their `beta.messages` counterparts, `beta.messages.tool_runner()`, and the per-request `params` of `messages.batches.create()` | `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` | Remove them. Current models do not use these sampling parameters; for an older model that still does, pass them through `extra_body` (see below).                                                                                                                                                                                          |
